pitfalls: A negative examination with incomplete visualisation does not exclude disease in the unseen region.
Pain location helps organise the search but does not independently prove the responsible organ or exclude alternative, remote or evolving pathology.

Compression, sonographic Murphy/tenderness, peristalsis and Doppler are not supplied by a static CT/MRI image or source colour; absent or inadequate acquisition remains unassessed.
Wall thickening, adjacent fat change, fluid and nodes overlap between causes; these patterns alone do not identify a pathogen, histological diagnosis, full disease extent or tissue viability.
A negative plain radiograph does not exclude fluid-filled obstruction or every acute abdominal process; projection is not resolved soft-tissue wall/organ anatomy.
Unacquired contrast phases, sequences, limited ultrasound windows or incomplete pelvic coverage cannot supply a complete vascular, organ, urinary or adnexal exclusion.

protocol: Record the actual modality, coverage, ECG synchronisation, cardiac phase, reconstruction thickness and motion limitations; use appropriately synchronised cross-sectional imaging for root/proximal ascending measurements.

measurements.name: Aortic annulus
measurements.method: Identify the virtual basal/hinge plane from the actual cusp attachment nadirs in multiplanar imaging; measure the annular contour and orthogonal dimensions in the stated phase. Record variant anatomy and unresolved nadirs.
measurements.pitfall: A fixed one-slice offset or the last visible leaflet is not a reproducible basal-plane definition; slice thickness, phase and cusp/valve morphology matter.

measurements.name: Sinus of Valsalva
measurements.method: Record the maximum sinus-to-sinus root diameter on the appropriate short-axis plane, with named edge convention and cardiac phase. Report multiple dimensions for an asymmetric root; retain any legacy average or alternative axis separately for comparison.
measurements.pitfall: Sinus-to-commissure, mid/maximum sinus-to-sinus and averages are not interchangeable; an average must not silently replace the maximum root diameter.

measurements.name: Thoracic aortic diameter
measurements.method: Use a plane perpendicular to the local aortic axis at every named level. For CT/MRI root and ascending assessment, record inner-edge measurements with ECG synchronisation; report outer-edge dimensions for abnormal thickened wall segments, retaining the actual convention.
measurements.pitfall: Axial slices cut the curved aorta obliquely and give elliptical, overestimated diameters.

measurements.name: Interval change
measurements.method: Compare the same level on the prior study using the same modality and method; give the change in millimetres and the interval.
measurements.pitfall: Small differences can reflect acquisition, phase, edge or plane variability; record comparability and uncertainty before assigning growth or applying clinical thresholds.

pitfalls: Raw axial sections may obliquely sample a curved aorta; retain orthogonal plane/centreline and selected level.
Edge conventions, cardiac phase and root-axis/summary method are not interchangeable; preserve maximal and asymmetric dimensions.
TTE leading-edge and CT/MRI inner/outer-edge methods have different conventions; document the actual method and patient/reference framework rather than treating all values as equivalent.
impression_prompts: What is the maximal diameter, at which level and by which method?
Is the aorta dilated against the sex-specific reference values used locally?
What has changed since the previous study measured the same way, and over what interval?
escalation: Communicate rapid growth, or a diameter at the local surgical threshold, to the referring team.

pitfalls: Hormonal activity cannot be excluded by benign imaging morphology.

Keep ESE/ENSAT 2023 recommendations separate from the Seow 2025 proposed pathway adopted by the updated source; record the framework and its incidentaloma/endocrine eligibility.

Routine excretory contrast in the bladder is not equivalent to a properly performed CT cystogram.
An early or limited CT cannot exclude every bowel, mesenteric, pancreatic duct or associated injury; retain injury timing, unavailable phases and unresolved interfaces.

Observed phase change must use actual corresponding anatomy, acquisition timing and blood-pool context. Absent growth or a single focal contrast appearance does not independently establish a contained vascular lesion or exclude active bleeding.
CT enhancement changes require actual acquired comparison and physiological context; a source colour or normal parent organ cannot establish perfusion, viability or infarction extent.

Free gas/fluid and a suspected tract require source-supported location and clinical interpretation; absent gas does not exclude contained or evolving injury, and dense clot does not independently prove its source.
A source-visible injury track, projected object or skin wound does not establish the full penetrating trajectory or every organ crossed; retain unresolved entry/exit and interfaces.

AAST revisions are organ-specific. The official resource lists renal 2025 and pancreatic 2024 revisions as well as the earlier 2018 spleen/liver/kidney revision; a generic 2018 label cannot supply every current scale. Numeric grade criteria require the actual applicable source and complete observations.

measurements.method: Measure source-resolved PA perpendicular to its local axis at a named level and source phase; use a stated ascending-aortic/reference measurement method and edge convention if ratio is reported.
measurements.pitfall: PA diameter/ratio alone does not diagnose haemodynamic PH or establish a clinical group; motion and contrast/coverage limits remain.

pitfalls: Absent contrast or severe motion is a technical limitation, not proof of occlusion or a negative embolic examination. Record affected segments and unresolved defect/mixing boundaries.

Acute emboli may be eccentric as well as central. No location/angle alone dates a clot or excludes acute-on-chronic disease; distinguish source filling defects from motion, mixing, partial-volume or other mimics.

CTEPD may occur without PH; CT chronic morphology alone does not establish CTEPH or operability. A limited or negative CTPA does not alone exclude distal chronic disease; clinical/perfusion assessment is separate.

CT dimensions, RV/LV, septal shape and reflux suggest morphology, not measured pressure or EF. In the named 2022 ESC/ERS definition PH requires resting mPAP >20 mmHg by haemodynamic source; precapillary pattern also requires PAWP ≤15 mmHg and PVR >2 WU. No such values are inferred from CT.

Emphysema/fibrosis, mosaic attenuation, septal thickening or a filling mass are differential clues, not automatic WHO-group, PVOD, sarcoma, infarct or viability diagnoses. Trace actual connections and retain clinical/tissue/functional uncertainty; no treatment choice is made from the companion model.

protocol: Confirm actually acquired views and source position, coverage, acquisition time and processing. Compare prior views with their own geometry/quality; missing lateral or other projections remain unavailable.

Review every covered central/peripheral/hidden interface systematically. Radiography is projection imaging: source silhouettes do not establish all native tissue boundaries, complete3D anatomy or clinical physiology.

checklist.label: Quality
checklist.detail: Record actual source projection, position, acquisition/coverage and quality; distinguish technical limitations and artefacts from disease.

checklist.label: Airways and mediastinum
checklist.detail: Inspect every covered airway, hilar, mediastinal and cardiac silhouette/interface with source projection limits; do not infer resolved chamber/wall anatomy or physiology from overlap.

checklist.label: Lungs
checklist.detail: Describe each actual pulmonary opacity/lucency, vascular or volume-change pattern and covered regional extent; assess hidden and overlapping areas with appropriate uncertainty.

checklist.label: Pleura
checklist.detail: Assess each actually visible pleural/diaphragmatic/recess interface and complication, with projection/position-dependent visibility and source limits.

checklist.label: Devices and review areas

measurements.name: Cardiothoracic ratio
measurements.method: Record actual cardiac/thoracic diameter method, acquired projection, position, inspiration and source calibration/uncertainty. Interpret only within a stated appropriate protocol.
measurements.pitfall: AP/supine magnification and low inspiration do not supply a comparable standard PA ratio or measured cardiac function.

measurements.name: Device tip distance
measurements.method: Use actual tip/port and named source landmark on a stated view/position with real calibration; record respiratory/temporal and overlap uncertainty.
measurements.pitfall: A projected distance or single view does not prove full3D intraluminal course, intended device function or unchanged position.

pitfalls: Technical correction, crop or annotation removal can change source presentation; preserve original source and disclose processing. An unavailable or limited view is not an adequately assessed negative study.

CTR interpretation requires the actual method and projection; AP/supine magnification or poor inspiration must not be treated as standard PA size. Silhouette enlargement does not measure pressure, EF, shunt or establish a unique cause.

Consolidation, oedema, infection, haemorrhage, collapse and malignancy can overlap. Air bronchograms or projected volume-loss signs support a differential, not unique pathology or microscopic confirmation.

An inconspicuous pneumothorax/effusion on a limited/supine film is not exclusion. Do not derive an exact fluid volume, tension physiology or fluid chemistry from one projection. Free gas/urgent findings require actual source and clinical assessment.

No device or complication is asserted absent until actual covered sources are assessed. Projected tip distances require named landmarks, phase/position and calibration; lumen/wall/3D course and dynamic function may remain unresolved.

escalation: Communicate suspected urgent pneumothorax, free gas, device complication or acute cardiopulmonary findings through local clinical pathways; tension/instability depends on actual source and clinical assessment.
